cases.rationale: Three actual people stand around the booth, and a brass bed frame with mattress/bedding is identifiable in front. The bag on the pink-shirted person's back/side has visible straps and a pack-like body, but the crop does not settle backpack (24) versus shoulder handbag (26), so both remain unclear. Small rectangular items on the rear shelves could be bound books (73), but their covers/spines cannot be distinguished confidently from display material. The draped display/work surfaces do not establish a dining table. I considered each of the 75 definitions and its exclusions against the whole crop; the remaining explicit no categories have no identifiable actual objects meeting their definitions.

An actual person in snow wears a compact black backpack with a contrasting striped panel and visible wearing context. Two narrow skis and ski poles are visible; they are not a snowboard, skateboard, or surfboard. Clothing and ski gloves do not meet the baseball-mitt definition. I considered each of the 75 definitions, including actual-object and exclusion rules, across this entire crop; no unresolved category ambiguity remains and no other category object is identifiable.

Actual pedestrians, passenger cars including the prominent dark SUV at the bottom, and traffic-signal heads at the right are identifiable. The prohibition sign is a no-left-turn sign, not a stop sign. Blue roadside equipment near the bottom could include bicycles (1), but wheels/frame details are too small to distinguish them from street fixtures confidently. The partly cropped yellow vehicle at the lower right and small distant large vehicles leave bus (5) versus truck (7) identity unresolved. I considered every one of the 75 definitions and common exclusions; the other explicit no categories lack identifiable actual objects.

The actual scissors have paired metal blades, a central pivot and orange handle portions. Their paired construction distinguishes them from a knife. The teal floral shapes are fabric decoration, not actual plants or animals. I explicitly considered each of the 75 definitions and common rules across the whole crop; no other listed actual object is present and no unresolved category ambiguity remains.

An actual helmeted person sits on a motor scooter whose windshield, powered body, seat and handlebar context identify motorcycle (3), rather than pedal bicycle. Passenger cars are visible behind the rider, and the tall white cargo-box road vehicle at the right supports truck (7). The rider's black back surface is clothing without an identifiable backpack. I considered all 75 exact definitions and common exclusions against the entire crop; no other listed object or unresolved category ambiguity remains.

The person at left stands beside an actual pedal bicycle with identifiable frame, saddle, rear rack and wheels. A white truck with a tall cab is visible at right, with a passenger car farther right. A small dark two-wheeler near that truck and the cropped foreground vehicle/mirror do not provide enough body detail to settle motorcycle (3), which remains unclear. The red street barrier is not a stop sign. I considered every one of the 75 definitions and exclusions; the remaining explicit no categories have no identifiable actual objects.

Two actual elephants are identifiable from their large heads, ears, legs and trunks, including the large curled trunk at center. Their anatomy excludes the other listed animal identities. The horizontal foreground piece is a rough wooden rail, without an identifiable multi-person seat or chair. I explicitly considered every one of the 75 definitions under the common rules; no other listed object or unresolved category ambiguity remains.

An actual person leans forward from a wooden single-person chair, with its seat/back and supports visible behind him. Actual pigeons stand and fly on the paved area. A separate long slatted wooden bench crosses the foreground; it is distinct from the person's chair. The grass is unpotted and the pavement/curb is not a table. I considered each of the 75 exact definitions and common exclusions; no other listed object is identifiable and no unresolved category ambiguity remains.

An actual tennis player holds a tennis racket with an identifiable oval strung head and handle, supported by the clay-court context. Wristbands and clothing are not gloves, ties or bags. The court and advertising borders supply no other listed actual objects. I explicitly considered all 75 exact definitions with the common rules; no unresolved category ambiguity remains.

The foreground human forearm and background people establish person. The blue pedal bicycle has identifiable frame, saddle, handlebars and wheels. The top edge includes an actual red octagonal stop-sign face with white border, although much is cropped. The foreground digital sports wristwatch leaves clock (74) unclear: its display may show elapsed exercise timing rather than time of day, and exercise timers are excluded. The padded black foreground object is a glove rather than a baseball fielding mitt. I considered all 75 definitions and common exclusions; other listed actual objects are not identifiable.

An actual person operates a white handheld game remote with a hanging strap in front of a standalone television on an open passenger SUV tailgate. The remote is supported by its handheld controller form and clear use context. A clear stemmed glass with bowl, slender stem and foot stands below the hand, meeting wine glass rather than cup. The large screen is a physical TV; the menu pictures inside it do not establish additional actual objects. Printed game packaging and the console are not identifiable bound books, laptops or keyboards, and the tailgate is not a dining table. I considered every one of the 75 definitions; no unresolved category ambiguity remains.

Several actual grazing horses are identifiable in the field from their equine heads, bodies, legs and tails. Their visible anatomy supports horse rather than cow, sheep or zebra. The rest of the crop is grassland, distant mountains and sky, without identifiable people, vehicles, furnishings or other listed actual objects. I explicitly considered each of the 75 exact definitions and common rules; no unresolved category ambiguity remains.
